comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Growth and Product Roadmap
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, AMD accelerated growth in its Data Center segment through strong demand for AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs, accelerated the AI accelerator roadmap to an annual cadence, and announced the 5th Gen AMD EPYC family.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD explicitly identify Data Center AI accelerators as a core, high-growth component of their compute businesses, though they reference different specific products. NVDA describes its Compute & Networking segment as comprising 'Data Center accelerated computing platforms,' while AMD highlights 'strong demand for our data center AI accelerator products' specifically identifying the 'AMD Instinct™ MI300X GPUs' as deployed by hyperscalers. Both disclosures frame this segment around high-performance computing for AI workloads, with AMD further noting an accelerated roadmap to deliver annual leadership solutions, paralleling NVDA's focus on its dominant AI infrastructure role.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.
The demand for our data center AI accelerator products was very strong as large hyperscaler customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed our AMD Instinct™ MI300X GPUs.
During the year, we announced that we have accelerated our AMD AI accelerator roadmap to deliver an annual cadence of leadership AMD Instinct solutions.

comparisons.peer_summary: VCF delivers integrated enterprise-class compute, networking, storage, management, and security across any environment, including native Kubernetes for VMs and containers, advanced AI/ML workloads support, and integrated data services.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose significant integration of networking capabilities into their core compute or infrastructure platforms. NVDA's Compute & Networking segment explicitly includes 'end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet.' Similarly, AVGO’s VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) is described as delivering 'integrated, enterprise-class compute, networking, storage... and VCF includes native Kubernetes... enables advanced AI and machine learning workloads at enterprise scale.' While NVDA focuses on the silicon/networking layer (InfiniBand/Ethernet) and AVGO focuses on the software-defined infrastructure layer (VCF), both identify the convergence of compute and networking to support advanced AI workloads as a key business driver.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.

• VCF: VCF delivers integrated, enterprise-class compute, networking, storage, management, and security across any environment. VCF includes native Kubernetes to support both virtual machines and containerized workloads on a single platform, enables advanced AI and machine learning workloads at enterprise scale and offers integrated data services capabilities. Our solutions enhance our customers' ability to continuously optimize performance and costs, protect the business from threats and enable the business to focus on outcomes instead of operations through advanced observability and insights.

comparisons.peer_topic: x86 Ecosystem Strategy and Advisory Group
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's core strategy relies on the x86 ecosystem, advancing it through microarchitectures focused on performance and efficiency. In 2024, the company created an advisory group to expand ecosystem compatibility, simplify software development, and identify future architectural needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and Intel describe their strategies as providing end-to-end compute and networking solutions that scale from the data center to the edge and include AI capabilities. NVDA lists its segment as comprising 'Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms.' Intel similarly states its product offerings 'provide end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI and autonomous driving.' Both disclosures emphasize a holistic 'end-to-end' approach to infrastructure that covers networking and data center compute for AI workloads.

Our product offerings provide end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI and autonomous driving, to serve an increasingly smart and connected world.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Compute and Networking Business Unit includes memory products and solutions for data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets, including HBM, DDR, LPDRAM, GDDR, CXL, and MRDIMM.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies include 'Networking' as a distinct and significant component of their business segment composition. NVDA's Item 1 defines its 'Compute & Networking segment' which comprises networking platforms. MU defines its 'Compute and Networking Business Unit (CNBU)' which includes memory products for data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets. While NVDA focuses on active networking hardware (switches/routers/AI fabric) and MU focuses on memory products for those markets, both explicitly structure their business reporting to reflect the synergy or distinct presence of computing and networking technologies.

sentences.text: The Compute & Networking segment is comprised of our Data Center accelerated computing platforms and end-to-end networking platforms including Quantum for InfiniBand and Spectrum for Ethernet; our NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform and automotive development agreements; Jetson robotics and other embedded platforms; NVIDIA AI Enterprise and other software; and DGX Cloud software and services.

CNBU includes memory products and solutions sold into the data center, PC, graphics, and networking markets including HBM, DDR, LPDRAM and GDDR, as well as some emerging memory technologies like compute express link ("CXL") and multi-ranked dual in-line memory module ("MRDIMM").

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is driving digital transformation in automotive via Snapdragon Digital Chassis platforms for connectivity and ADAS/AD, and in IoT across consumer, edge networking, and industrial applications such as PCs, tablets, and logistics.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the inclusion of automotive platforms in their business composition, though the nature of the technology differs significantly. NVDA includes its 'NVIDIA DRIVE automated-driving platform' within its Compute & Networking segment. QCOM drives digital transformation in 'automotive via Snapdragon Digital Chassis platforms for connectivity and ADAS/AD.' While both touch on automotive ADAS/autonomous driving, NVDA's inclusion is part of a broader AI/Compute portfolio, whereas QCOM's is a primary expansion area distinct from its legacy mobile business. The comparison is related rather than same-topic because NVDA's automotive offering is a subset of its broader data-center-focused compute strategy, while QCOM's automotive strategy is a major standalone growth vector distinct from any data-center compute focus.

We are scaling our innovations across industries and applications beyond mobile handsets, driving digital transformation with our ecosystem partners in areas including automotive and the internet of things (IoT).

In automotive, our Snapdragon® Digital Chassis™ platforms, including connectivity, digital cockpit and advanced driver assistance and automated driving (ADAS/AD), are helping to connect the car to its environment and the cloud, creating unique in-cabin experiences and enabling a comprehensive assisted and automated driving solution.
